svg.title: The free stabilizer point and the intrinsic stack-point adjunction
svg.desc: A lowest-degree formal Hopf relation would be additive and contradict characteristic zero, so complex finite-type stabilizers are smooth. Their perfect de Rham cochains C have derived dual algebra B. The full groupoid and module bars agree with products retained, identifying Dmod(BA) with B-modules and actual point restriction with forgetting. The free module B is compact and regular. Locally closed and open extension gives the intrinsic point delta representing extraordinary restriction on every unbounded operator target. The constant module on the multiplicative stabilizer is not compact. Nonzero rational functions on the affine line have all closed-point extraordinary fibres zero, so point adjunction alone is not a generator theorem.
svg.text: The free stabilizer point and the intrinsic stack-point adjunction
Complex bundle points; every curve genus and reductive component; full unbounded targets.
1. Smooth stabilizer and actual residual gerbe — SPT.1–SPT.6
Formal relation: fᵣ(x+y)=fᵣ(x)+fᵣ(y) ⇒ (2ʳ−2)fᵣ=0.
Characteristic zero excludes every least relation of order r≥2.
pt → BA → U=[Z/H] → Y=Bun(G), y = j i q.
The orbit H/A is smooth and locally closed; the orbit map is an actual A-torsor.
2. Perfect cochains and the entire mapping bar — SPT.7–SPT.13
C(A)=RHom(Dmod(A))(ω,ω), B(A)=C(A) dual.
RHom(Aⁿ)(ω⊗V,ω⊗W) = RHom(C)(B(A)⊗ⁿ ⊗ V,W).
Groupoid transport ↔ Hopf coaction ↔ B(A)-module action.
Dmod(BA) ≃ Mod(B(A)), q! = forgetful functor.
The two full mapping totalizations coincide; all products and higher maps are retained.
3. The free point and its exact atlas shift — SPT.14–SPT.16
Left adjoint to q!: q_!(V) = B(A) ⊗ V in the module model.
RHom(BA)(q_!C,F) = q!F: the free point is compact.
Unnormalized atlas: V=q!F. Cartan atlas: V[−dim A].
The free point has Cartan value B(A)[−dim A], not the constant augmentation.
On Gₘ: B=Λ(ε), |ε|=−1; the free point has degrees −1,0.
4. Actual extension and intrinsic adjunction — SPT.17–SPT.24
RHom(Y)(δ(y)!,M) = y!M for every unbounded operator M.
Coherent biduality proves the open adjunction on compact coherent tests.
Full compact bars and smooth mapping-complex descent extend it to every target.
Continuity of y! ⇒ compact δ(y)!; its chart coefficients are bounded regular.
5. Exact distinctions — SPT.25–SPT.33
Π(δ(y)!) is ind-regular by CDK.25; no generator conclusion follows yet.
On BGₘ: free B is compact; the constant C has Ext(C,C)=C[u], |u|=2.
In characteristic p, αₚ has relation xᵖ: its additive leading term is allowed.
On A¹: C(x) ≠ 0, but [C(x) —(x−a)→ C(x)] = 0 for every a∈C.
C(x) is a filtered colimit of regular holonomic finite-pole connections.
Exact proofs: §§3.253–3.263, SPT.1–SPT.33; Solutions3.DY,3.DZ,3.EA.
The half twist retains its actual point-fibre line and its Morita equivalence.
Enhanced nilpotent generation and the support criterion remain separate arguments.
Point adjunction and regular-input preservation alone do not prove full-image regularity.
All groupoid comparisons use actual group multiplication, identity and inversion.
